                    ### Question
                    Does it indicate which of the following statements in reference to factor V of Leiden is true?

                    ### Options
                    opa. It is the resistance of factor V to the action of protein S.
opb. It is an acquired disorder that is associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies.
opc. Its presence causes a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time.
opd. Together with the prothrombin mutation, it constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition in our environment.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Factor V Leiden is a genetic mutation that leads to resistance to activated protein C, not protein S, and is not associated with anticardiolipin antibodies, making option opa incorrect. It is not an acquired disorder, thus option opb is incorrect. Factor V Leiden does not cause a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time, so option opc is incorrect. Together with the prothrombin mutation, Factor V Leiden is one of the most common genetic-based thrombotic predispositions, supporting option opd as the correct statement. The retrieved evidence path supports the association of activated protein C with thrombosis, aligning with the consensus that Factor V Leiden increases thrombotic risk due to resistance to activated protein C.
